explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Paul says all things were created in the Son, "…things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible…" (Colossians 1:16). That covers what you can see and what you can't. I once spent years in the dark of a junk drawer, and even there, nothing was outside what He made.
Close, friend, but Paul goes bigger. He says "…things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible…" (Colossians 1:16). So the earth is in there, and so is heaven. Paul keeps the list wide open.

Paul doesn't narrow it down like that, friend. He says "…all things were created…" in Him, and he lists "…things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible…" (Colossians 1:16). That's way more than creatures. Paul's list is wide: heaven, earth, seen and unseen.

Not quite, baker. Paul names "…thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities." and then says "All things were created through Him and for Him." (Colossians 1:16). Nothing on that list was made apart from the Son. Even the big powers with the big titles are on the Son's side of the counter.

Right, baker. Paul lists thrones, dominions, rulers and authorities, and then says "All things were created through Him and for Him." (Colossians 1:16). Not one of those powers was made apart from Him. Big titles, same Maker.

Yes, baker. Paul says the Son "…is before all things, and in Him all things hold together." (Colossians 1:17). Both halves are in the same verse. The Son comes first, and in Him all things hold together.

Look at the second half of the verse, friend. Paul says, "He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together." (Colossians 1:17). So he says both. The Son comes first, and in Him everything holds together.

explanations.answer: So He has first place in all things
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Paul says it's "…so that in all things He may have preeminence." (Colossians 1:18). Preeminence means first place. The Son is the head of the body, the beginning, the firstborn from among the dead, and Paul ties all of that to this one purpose.

explanations.answer: So the church grows in number
explanations.explanation: The church is in the verse, friend, since the Son is its head. But the purpose Paul gives is a different one: "…so that in all things He may have preeminence." (Colossians 1:18). That means first place in everything. Paul doesn't mention the church growing in number here.

explanations.answer: So the prophets are proven true
explanations.explanation: Good thought, but Paul doesn't say that here. He gives the purpose in the same verse: "…so that in all things He may have preeminence." (Colossians 1:18). Preeminence means first place. The prophets don't come up in these verses.
Not this time, baker. Paul says "…God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him…" (Colossians 1:19). All of it, with no part held back. So "only part" doesn't match what Paul wrote.
Right, baker. Paul says "…God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him…" (Colossians 1:19). The word is ALL. Nothing is left out.

explanations.answer: Through the blood of His cross
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says God reconciles all things to Himself "…by making peace through the blood of His cross." (Colossians 1:20). The peace comes through the cross. Paul says it plainly, and I never get tired of hearing it.

explanations.answer: Through the law given at Sinai
explanations.explanation: The law at Sinai is a fair guess, friend, but Paul doesn't point there for this peace. He says God reconciles all things "…by making peace through the blood of His cross." (Colossians 1:20). The peace he names is through the cross.
Paul doesn't point there in this verse, friend. He says the peace is made "…through the blood of His cross." (Colossians 1:20). That's the way he names, and he doesn't list another.

Not quite, baker. Paul says "Once you were alienated from God and were hostile in your minds, engaging in evil deeds." (Colossians 1:21). That's the opposite of close and at peace. He's describing how far off things stood before.

Right, baker. Paul says "Once you were alienated from God and were hostile in your minds, engaging in evil deeds." (Colossians 1:21). Alienated means far away, not close. Paul is honest about where they started.

That's right, baker. Paul says "…He has reconciled you by Christ’s physical body through death to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence…" (Colossians 1:22). Three words, and each one is good news. Paul says it, so I'll say it loud.

This one is in the text, friend. Paul says He has reconciled them "…to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence…" (Colossians 1:22). That's the reason he gives. All three words are right there.

explanations.answer: The hope of the gospel they heard
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says to continue "…established and firm, not moved from the hope of the gospel you heard…" (Colossians 1:23). That's the hope they heard in the gospel. Stay put, friend, because a stamper who stays pressed down makes a clean cookie.

Paul doesn't point there, friend. He says not to be "…moved from the hope of the gospel you heard…" (Colossians 1:23). The hope they're to hold onto is in the gospel. Elders and their traditions aren't in this verse.

explanations.answer: The law handed down by Moses
explanations.explanation: Fair guess, friend, but Paul doesn't name the law here. He says not to be moved "…from the hope of the gospel you heard…" (Colossians 1:23). The gospel is what they heard, so that's what he says to hold onto.

That's right, baker. Paul says the gospel "…has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven, and of which I, Paul, have become a servant." (Colossians 1:23). Paul is a servant, and he says so himself. I think that's a humble way to put it.
Not quite, friend. Paul says, "…of which I, Paul, have become a servant." (Colossians 1:23). He doesn't call himself a judge. A servant serves, and that's the word he picked.
Good guess, but Paul goes the other way. He says, "…of which I, Paul, have become a servant." (Colossians 1:23). A master gives orders, and a servant serves. Paul chose servant.
